title: Inside Amitabh Bachchan's Fitness Routine at 83: Pranayama, Plant-Based Diet, and a Mindset His Trainers Call Unmatched
excerpt: The megastar's long-time wellness trainer reveals the daily discipline behind Bollywood's most enduring career.
body:
Breathwork Before Everything

At 83, Amitabh Bachchan remains one of the busiest actors in Indian cinema — shooting films, hosting Kaun Banega Crorepati, and maintaining a prolific social media presence. The secret, according to Vrinda Bhatt, who has served as his wellness trainer for over 25 years, is deceptively simple: controlled breathing.

"My sessions with Amit ji are more about breathwork," Bhatt told Humans of Bombay. "We start off with basic breath exercises and move on to pranayams, and basic yoga stretches. Mindset — he's the father of it all."

Bachchan begins each morning with pranayama, the yogic breathing practice that enhances lung capacity, strengthens the heart, reduces stress, and improves digestion. He has maintained this daily ritual without fail for years, Bhatt said — a consistency that has become the foundation of his physical resilience.

Discipline That Puts Younger Actors to Shame

Shivohaam, another member of Bachchan's training team, described an actor whose commitment to fitness borders on obsessive. "There are times when we have to tell him not to train right now," Shivohaam said. Bachchan would squeeze in exercise between meetings, before shoots, and late in the evening — prompting his trainers to occasionally intervene when the timing could interfere with sleep and recovery.

"If Mr. Bachchan can make time to exercise, regular people can, of course, take out time to exercise."

— Vrinda Bhatt, Amitabh Bachchan's wellness trainer

"Whether it's morning, afternoon, or evening, or even between meetings, he does remove time," Shivohaam said. "So if he can schedule things according to that, I am pretty sure that other people can also, if they want to."

When Bhatt first started training Bachchan, sessions began at 6 a.m. He was never late. "He taught me the value of time," she said.

A Plant-Based Diet Without Compromise

Bachchan follows a disciplined vegetarian diet that he documents on his personal blog. His mornings begin with tulsi (basil) leaves, known for their immunity-boosting and blood-pressure-regulating properties. Breakfast typically includes a protein shake, almonds, porridge or oatmeal, and coconut water, supplemented with gooseberry (amla) juice and dates.

The strict eliminations are notable: no sugar, no rice, and no non-vegetarian food. All meals are home-cooked and consumed in moderation. His trainers credit this dietary discipline, paired with consistent yoga and pranayama, for maintaining his energy levels through gruelling 12-hour shoot days that would tax actors half his age.

What the Diaspora Can Take From It

Bachchan's approach is rooted in traditional Indian wellness practices — pranayama, yoga, tulsi, amla — that are increasingly validated by Western scientific research. His routine requires no expensive gym membership or exotic supplements. It is a reminder that the foundations of longevity are available to anyone willing to show up at 6 a.m. and breathe.
nri_angle: Bachchan's yoga-and-pranayama-first approach to longevity resonates with diaspora interest in traditional Indian wellness practices.
